about: Marches on an enemy castle or town, waits near it for the named lords if you give any, then besieges it. You choose who decides when to storm (storm): the game's own commander, a bar of engines built and strength that you set, or nobody (starve them out). You also set, when you give the order, the relief that makes it storm at once and the relief that makes it withdraw: it acts on them the hour it sees them, without waiting for your answer. A camp can never storm before its preparations are done (the game's rule).
calls_back: enemy lords and armies near it or heading for it, counted together, are strong enough to matter (and again each time they grow by half its strength), it storms or withdraws by your relief bars, the siege is won, or it is broken

wait_hours: how long to wait near it for the named lords
relief_ratio: call back when the enemy lords and armies within relief_radius of it or heading for it from anywhere, all counted together, reach this many times its strength
relief_radius: how near counts for the relief, in map units (those seen heading for it count wherever they are)
storm: who decides the storm: 0 the game's own commander (once the camp's preparations are done it tries about three times an hour, the likelier the more the besiegers outweigh the defenders with their walls); 1 storm as soon as the preparations are done, storm_engines siege engines are built and the besiegers are storm_ratio times the defenders; 2 do not storm (starve them out) unless storm_on_relief says so
storm_engines: with storm 1: the siege engines the camp must have built before it storms (0: the moment the preparations are done)
storm_ratio: with storm 1: storm only once the besiegers' strength is at least this many times the defenders' (0: no bar)
storm_on_relief: storm as soon as the camp may once the relief due within relief_hours, all counted together, reaches this many times its strength (0: never)
withdraw_on_relief: lift the siege and march into the nearest of your castles or towns once the relief due within relief_hours reaches this many times its strength (0: never); weighed before storm_on_relief
relief_hours: the relief counted for those two bars: the enemy lords and armies near it or heading for it that would get there within this many hours, by the game's marching rules

when.poke: {at} is no longer an enemy holding.
{at} is no longer an enemy holding.
{me} waited {wait_hours} hours near {at}; {lords_arrived()} of {lords_count()} lords came. Besieging now.
{at} is no longer an enemy holding.

when.if: hours_in_state > 6 and not besieging and not within(at, 3)
withdraw_on_relief > 0 and relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius) >= strength * withdraw_on_relief
when.poke: {me} lifts the siege of {at} by your bar: the relief due within {relief_hours} hours is strength {relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius)} together, at least {withdraw_on_relief} times its {strength}. It marches into {nearest_fort()}. Nearest first: {relief_of(at, relief_radius)}.

when.if: storm_on_relief > 0 and storm_now == 0 and relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius) >= strength * storm_on_relief
when.poke: {me} storms {at} as soon as the camp may, by your bar: the relief due within {relief_hours} hours is strength {relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius)} together, at least {storm_on_relief} times its {strength}. {storm_text(at)} Nearest first: {relief_of(at, relief_radius)}.

when.if: relief_coming(at, relief_radius) >= pick(relief_told > 0, relief_told + strength * 0.5, strength * relief_ratio)
when.poke: A relief is coming to {at}: {relief_count(at, relief_radius)} enemy lords and armies within {relief_radius} of it or heading for it, strength {relief_coming(at, relief_radius)} together, against {me}'s {strength}. Nearest first: {relief_of(at, relief_radius)}. {storm_text(at)}
{me} lifted the siege of {at}, but no castle or town of yours is free to withdraw into; it holds where it is. Give it an order.
{me} is inside {refuge}, out of the relief's way. Its next order does not start; give it one.
